blockers.symptom: The full MySQL verification profile reached 60 integration tests but four session test contexts failed to start with MySQL error 1040: Too many connections.
blockers.reproduction: Run the full .\mvnw.cmd -B -ntp -Dmaven.repo.local=.local/m2 -Pmysql-it verify profile with the uncapped test Hikari pools.
blockers.suspected_cause: Cached Spring integration-test contexts retain multiple Hikari pools at the default size; their combined connections exceed the local MySQL limit.

attempts.hypothesis: Cached Spring test contexts exhaust the local MySQL connection limit through uncapped default Hikari pools.
attempts.action: Set spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=4 only in Maven Surefire/Failsafe test processes; rerun the failed full profile and focused session/result regression.
attempts.outcome: Both gates passed with no errors or skips; production datasource configuration was unchanged.

blockers.safe_alternative: Cap Hikari pool size only for Maven test processes; keep production datasource sizing unchanged.
blockers.next_action: Resolved in V0034; keep the test-only cap and retain the original failure log.

blockers.suspected_cause: A cached ClosedBrowserExpiryIT context retained a 100 ms scheduled scan with a future fixed Clock and finalized later real-time recovery fixtures in the shared isolated integration schema; other fixed-clock contexts also retained periodic scans.

attempts.hypothesis: A cached 100 ms fixed-clock expiry test scheduler was finalizing later real-time recovery fixtures in the shared integration schema.
attempts.action: Set a one-hour scheduler default only in Maven test processes, close the intentional fast-scheduler context after its class, derive recovery fixture time from the injected Clock, then rerun the original full profile and adjacent ordered regression.
attempts.outcome: The original full gate passed 14 unit/HTTP and 63 MySQL integration tests; the ordered adjacent gate passed 14 plus 21, with no failures/errors/skips. Production scheduling remains 15 seconds.

blockers.next_action: Resolved in V0037; retain the original failed log and passing reruns.

blockers.symptom: The generic with_server helper declared TCP 8080 ready, but the first /api/csrf request timed out after ten seconds; its cleanup left the Java child process running.
blockers.reproduction: Run .local/dashboard-run-with-server.py using the generic webapp-testing with_server.py helper against the packaged demo and isolated online_exam_e2e schema.
blockers.suspected_cause: The helper starts a shell, captures Java stdout/stderr in undrained PIPEs, checks only TCP readiness, and terminates the shell rather than its Windows Java child. A direct Java process with file-backed output and HTTP readiness avoids these observed runner weaknesses.

attempts.hypothesis: Undrained server output plus shell-based Windows lifecycle prevents usable HTTP readiness and cleanup.
attempts.action: Use structured Java process arguments, direct file output, HTTP /api/ready polling and direct process termination for this isolated test runner.
attempts.outcome: V0055 passed the original keyboard/authentication check plus offline, safe-text, expiry and 16 desktop/mobile layout regressions. Direct Java process stopped cleanly; local development app restarted successfully.

blockers.safe_alternative: Directly manage this isolated local Java test process without changing application security or database behavior.
blockers.next_action: Resolved; use python tools/run_dashboard_checks.py for these isolated Windows browser checks.

attempts.outcome: The original package check passed after the guarded owned-process stop. Final package, 14 unit/HTTP, 69 MySQL, four browser cases, native acceptance, restart and clean setup all passed; live data matched and the updated owned app restarted successfully.
